name: JSW Dulux Ltd
title: JSW Dulux Ltd - 500710 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: JSW Dulux Q2 FY27 volume rose ~21.8% and revenue ~21.3%, but gross margin fell ~400 bps on industrial price-cost lag, leaving EBITDA margin near 11.5%.
summary.overview: Comparable like-to-like revenue grew about 21.3% with volume up about 21.8%, helped by a bounce in undercoats and share gains in decorative and industrial. Price rose about 7.9% but adverse mix of about 8.4% offset it, and industrial price hikes lagged crude-linked raw material inflation. EBITDA was INR110.9 crore (up 4.4% vs like-to-like INR106.3 crore) and PAT before exceptionals was INR71.2 crore (up 2% from INR69.8 crore), with the tax rate near 19% helped by a one-off release. Management kept the ~13-14% EBITDA margin aim as an intent only, since full-year guidance is no longer valid given elevated crude and INR around 94.5-96/USD.

financial_highlights.change: YoY; excludes ~INR24.3 crore of revenue transferred to AkzoNobel unlisted entity and intercompany decorative sales that no longer continue
Lower due to one-off release of excess tax provision (AY 2013-14 favourable order)

financial_highlights.value: ~60% decorative / ~40% industrial (stated as 57%-43% in one answer)

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Mid-double-digit revenue growth and high-single-digit premium volume growth in H1; ex-putty and texture volume grew about 8-8.5%, with undercoats a seasonal boost. Margin held roughly flat sequentially; cumulative price increases about 3.2-3.5% plus a further ~1% announced for November.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue and volume grew about 32% and high-double-digit respectively, with new accounts and share gains in coil coating, packaging and vehicle refinish. Raw material COGS rose about 30-35% in marine, protective, coil and packaging vs price hikes of ~6-7%; industrial EBITDA margin now high single-digit, with a ~4% industrial price increase announced.

guidance_outlook: Management intends to get close to 13% EBITDA margin (earlier 13-14% guidance) but said full-year target is no longer valid; H2 target depends on crude and INR/USD.
Expects industrial margins to recover as price increases flow through; said the margin pressure is temporary, not structural.
Working capital elevated from TiO2 pre-buy and industrial credit delays; expects return to normal levels over 3-5 months.
Project Akshaya targeted to contribute roughly 7-10% of full-year EBITDA; ERP consolidation expected around December 2026.
Expects H2 demand to remain buoyant if crude and dollar do not worsen; monitoring rainfall deficit and price pass-through through November-December.
capex_capacity: Industrial capacity utilisation in some verticals near 75%, leading to higher industrial capex earlier in the year.
Additional decorative capacity being evaluated by segment demand; continued spend on tinting machines and Dulux stores.

Cross-manufacturing started across five JSW Dulux plants and three JSW Paints plants (e.g., JSW Paints made in Mohali and Hyderabad; JSW Dulux made in Vijayanagar); additional capex flagged but not quantified.
No incentives or tax benefits expected from cross-manufacturing; existing plants have largely used available benefits.
demand_pricing: Price hikes staggered in three tranches (30 September, 14 October, 26 October) versus most competitors' 1 November, to help smaller dealers absorb them; blended price exit rate in September 10.4% vs quarterly average 7.9%.
Decorative cumulative price increase about 13.5% by management's count (including the antidumping-related 2%), with a further 1% announced for November.
Competitive intensity in activation and discounting continues, somewhat lower than two years ago; pricing discipline improved as most players took hikes.
Share gains in decorative regained after last year's losses, with growth more broad-based (North and West earlier; South improving; East still a challenge).
Growth split between own stores and new stores moved to about 55%-45% in favour of existing stores (previously ~70-30 towards new stores).
Management said it is not seeing a demand slowdown in retail or projects; October was strong, though it is unclear how much growth is price-led versus demand-led.
Crude fell back to about $105-106/bbl from a peak of ~$114 (~$95 when budget set); INR/USD about 94.5 after touching 96.

qa_highlights.question: How will industrial coatings profitability evolve in FY27, given lower price hikes and higher crude sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Marine, protective, coil and packaging COGS rose ~30-35% vs price hikes of ~6-7%, causing a lag; industrial EBITDA margin is now high single-digit and management is pushing price and pruning low-margin accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%+ volume growth driven by market share gains, and where?
qa_highlights.answer: Gains in vehicle refinish, coil and packaging; holding in marine. Decorative has regained share lost last year; growth broadening, with the South improving and East still a challenge.

qa_highlights.question: How should capex and incremental spend be viewed given 20%+ volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Cross-manufacturing across JSW Dulux and JSW Paints plants has started; industrial capex was stepped up as utilisation approached 75%, and decorative capacity is being assessed by segment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 FY27 outlook given the rainfall deficit?
qa_highlights.answer: Rainfall deficit is within range at the aggregate level; no demand slowdown seen in retail or projects; H2 demand expected to stay buoyant if crude and the dollar do not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the tax rate about 19% and what is the full-year rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower rate due to a one-off release of an excess tax provision after a favourable order for AY 2013-14; full-year rate should return to about 25.6%.

qa_highlights.question: Is competitive intensity easing, and how is JSW Dulux responding?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes taken by most players so discipline is better, but activation and discounting remain intense, slightly lower than before; management says execution excellence and integration are the focus.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the working capital build and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built from a titanium dioxide pre-buy and market credit stress mainly in industrial; expected to normalise over the next 3-5 months.

qa_highlights.question: What share of gross margin savings and Akshaya contribution is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshaya savings are on target, with INR7.3 crore realised in Q2; full-year target is roughly 7-10% of EBITDA, and targets are not being disclosed quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Where is industrial growth coming from, and what new segments are being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Automotive is the focus as the vehicle parc grows about 20% CAGR; management is looking at higher-margin segments that can be entered over the next year, provided they are not margin-dilutive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin path to 13-15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year guidance is not valid; intent is to get close to 13%. Further lift is expected from integration across procurement, manufacturing and functions with JSW Paints.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery in industrial depends on the pace of price pass-through against crude-linked raw material inflation (COGS up ~30-35% in some verticals).
Crude at about $105-115 and INR/USD near 94.5-96 may keep input costs elevated; management said it cannot predict the H2 margin.
Rainfall deficit in some states and whether recent price hikes (decorative cumulative ~13.5%) dent demand in November-December.
Growth quality: volume growth partly from undercoats and a seasonal bounce; unclear how much is price-led.
Adverse mix from faster industrial growth and de-weighting of low-margin accounts.
Working capital (TiO2 pre-buy inventory and industrial receivables) to normalise over the next 3-5 months.
Execution risk on the Akshaya integration and ERP go-live around December 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and revenue momentum but cautious on margins, with management repeatedly describing the gross margin hit as temporary and tied to crude and the rupee. Evasive on FY27 full-year margin guidance and on tax-benefit questions, stating that full-year targets are no longer valid.
key_quotes: So it's a bit of tale of two stories, high volume growth, high revenue growth.
We believe that, look, it's a bit of a short-term issue, which we start to correct, right?
And hence, the gross margin dilution of the industrial business impact is significant more on Dulux, which is not structural, it's temporary.

Our target EBITDA in the second half because full year now is not valid because the -- see, when we made the -- when I gave you a 13% to 14%, as I mentioned, the crude was at $95 and the dollar was at INR95

adds.what: Additional decorative capacity being evaluated (not quantified)
Cross-manufacturing across five JSW Dulux and three JSW Paints plants (additional capex flagged, not quantified)

growth.why: Management softened the EBITDA margin aim to 'close to 13%' for H2 FY27 and said the full-year target is no longer valid; Q2 like-to-like revenue grew ~21.3% and volume ~21.8%, backed by price hikes, share gains and undercoat seasonality rather than quantified new capacity, with industrial utilisation near 75% in some verticals and extra capex flagged but not sized.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management intends to get close to 13% EBITDA margin (cut from 13-14%) and calls the industrial gross margin hit temporary, but Q2 EBITDA margin was ~11.5% and full-year guidance is no longer valid given crude near $105-106/bbl and INR at 94.5-96/USD.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Cross-manufacturing across five JSW Dulux and three JSW Paints plants has already started, but new decorative capacity is only being evaluated and is not quantified, with no dated plant commissioning in the call.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volume grew ~21.8% in Q2 on share gains and undercoat seasonality, and management expects H2 demand to stay buoyant if crude and the dollar do not worsen, though it is unclear how much growth is price-led (blended price 7.9%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Industrial utilisation has reached about 75% in some verticals, management says it is going to 'beef up investments' with higher industrial capex, and decorative capacity is being evaluated, though no amount is quantified.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Full-year guidance was withdrawn as no longer valid, and the H2 margin target was narrowed to 'close to 13%' with crude and INR/USD cited as uncontrollable headwinds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Full-year guidance is already withdrawn, and gross margin fell ~400 bps with industrial COGS up ~30-35% against price hikes of ~6-7%, so further cuts depend on crude and INR staying elevated.

rows.label: Further price increases to pass through input costs
rows.why: Decorative cumulative price increase is about 13.5% with a further 1% from November, and industrial price up ~4% announced, though industrial hikes (~6-7%) have lagged COGS inflation of ~30-35%.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation after TiO2 pre-buy
rows.why: Working capital is elevated from the TiO2 pre-buy and industrial credit delays, and management expects a return to normal levels over 3-5 months.

rows.label: Project Akshaya savings and ERP go-live
rows.why: Akshaya realised INR7.3 crore in Q2 and targets roughly 7-10% of full-year EBITDA, with ERP consolidation expected around December 2026.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume and revenue momentum, and on pricing discipline, but cautious on margins and evasive on full-year guidance, while analysts pressed on the gross margin hit, price-led versus demand-led growth, and tax-benefit quality.
